record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that there is a connected countable dense homogeneous subspace X of the plane R^2 that is meager-in-itself?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Is there consistently a connected CDH X ⊆ R2 which is meager-in-itself?

artifact.self_contained_problem: A separable metrizable space $X$ is said to be countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$ there is a homeomorphism $h\colon X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. A topological space is meager-in-itself if it is of the first Baire category as a subspace of itself (equivalently, it is a countable union of subsets each of which is nowhere dense in $X$). Working in ZFC, decide whether the following statement is consistent: there exists a connected subspace $X$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $X$ is countable dense homogeneous and $X$ is meager-in-itself.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in the literature on countable dense homogeneity. Related work characterizes meager-in-itself CDH metric spaces via λ-sets and establishes consistency results about their cardinality, but no construction or impossibility result for a connected meager-in-itself CDH subspace of the plane appears in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and λ-sets
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of a meager-in-itself CDH metric space of size κ is equivalent to existence of a λ-set of size κ.
status_evidence.claim: The meager-in-itself CDH question is tied to λ-sets, but the connected planar version remains unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Nearly Countable Dense Homogeneous Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of CDH spaces, meager and Baire cases, with consistency results on cardinality.
status_evidence.claim: No construction of a connected meager-in-itself CDH planar subspace is reported.
